headline: Rise in US 10-year yield driven by higher neutral rate and strong growth, not fiscal term-premium blow-out — bond Armageddon narrative likely overdone
reasoning: Decomposing the US 10-year yield into risk-neutral and term-premium components, the rise has come from the risk-neutral side rather than the term premium, where fiscal concerns would normally show up. This suggests the market is lifting its estimate of where policy rates will settle long term, reflecting both slightly higher inflation volatility and a stronger underlying US growth trajectory. AI-driven productivity gains are supporting a higher trend growth rate, which means higher rates are compatible with strong equity earnings rather than being a headwind.
quote: When you decompose the US 10 year yield in terms of the risk neutral and also the term premium, the rise in the 10 year bond yield hasn't really come from the term premium. That's where you'd expect the fiscal concerns to actually show up. So what's actually coming through is on the risk neutral side and really where policy rates are going to be in a longer term sense for the US economy. Now, why are markets lifting up where they think rates are going to be? Some of it is due to maybe inflation being a little bit more volatile. So therefore you need to lift rates, but also the growth trajectory for the US economy is actually relatively strong. And so in that sense, if rates are only responding to a higher neutral rate because the trend growth rate in the economy is so much stronger, productivity is lifting because of AI, then a lot of the bond Armageddon comments that a lot of commentators put out there may actually not come to fruition.
